text:
sam: heads up — our generated python SDK has weak types for the "stream_chat" endpoint and it's breaking pyright in some customers' sample apps. minimal repro attached.

sam: snippet:
```python
from redwood import Client

client = Client()

async def consumer():
    async for part in client.chat.stream(prompt="hello"):
        # expecting `.delta.text`, but pyright complains
        print(part.delta.text)
```

sam: pyright error: "Property 'delta' not found on type 'dict'" — generator currently types stream return as `AsyncIterator[Dict[str, Any]]`.
maria: hmm. we fell back to generic dict for streaming because codegen didn't emit per-event models. is there a reason we didn't create ChatStreamEvent model earlier?
sam: seems generator treats streaming responses as opaque sequences.

ryan: quick fixes we can ship: 1) emit explicit ChatStreamEvent dataclass/pydantic model and type the stream as `AsyncIterator[ChatStreamEvent]`; 2) ship a small `redwood_sdk-stubs` package with .pyi files so static checkers get proper signatures; 3) update the sample app docs with a short-term cast example.
maria: casting example customers can use now: `from typing import cast, AsyncIterator; async for e in cast(AsyncIterator[ChatStreamEvent], client.chat.stream(...)):` — not ideal but it's a stopgap. add it to docs. :+1:

sam: another compatibility snag: some typing helpers we're tempted to use (ParamSpec, Concatenate) are awkward on py3.8. a subset of customers still run 3.8. we can't break them.

ryan: options: generate simpler signatures that only use typing available on 3.8, and keep richer typings in .pyi files that are only used by type checkers. That way runtime wheel stays py3.8-compatible.
maria: yeah, we can guard imports under TYPE_CHECKING to reference typing_extensions when needed. also ensure `from __future__ import annotations` in generated modules to reduce forward-ref issues.
sam: packaging question — should stubs be included in the normal wheel (as .pyi next to modules) or a separate `redwood-sdk-stubs` distribution? separate stubs let folks opt in, but bundling them simplifies things for most users. any preference?

ryan: separate package might be easier to iterate on without forcing a runtime release. but pyright and mypy both pick up bundled .pyi files automatically if present in the package. maybe start with bundled .pyi and switch to external if iteration frequency becomes painful.
maria: also, how do we model end-of-stream events? Currently generator sometimes emits `Union[Chunk, FinalEvent]` which makes consumers have to union-check. that triggers a ton of `isinstance` in sample code. I'd prefer a single event model with optional `done: bool` field or `type: Literal['delta','done']` to keep consumers ergonomic.
sam: agreed, simpler model is better for DX. please put that in the RFC.

ci-bot: <ci> test-suite failed on branch streaming-types-fix (mypy: error: "Dict[str, Any]" has no attribute "delta")</ci>

ryan: I'll prototype generator changes to emit ChatStreamEvent and add a basic .pyi for the stream API. plan: parse schema -> emit dataclass signature -> write .pyi into package during build. target: demo PR by EOD tomorrow.
maria: I'll add a short doc PR with the cast workaround and a note about pinned python versions. we should also add a test that runs mypy/pyright on the sample app to catch regressions.
sam: thanks. please also include a short migration note for users who rely on `dict`-style streaming objects (we'll keep runtime shape stable but add typed wrappers).

ryan: noted. attaching my local repro to the issue now. will post updates in this thread.
sam: awesome, cheers everyone. :rocket:
